_meta.indication: APTIOM is indicated as adjunctive treatment of partial-onset seizures (in patients with epilepsy 18 years and older).
_meta.receipt_date: Submission date: 02/11/2013 (complete response resubmission); original NDA received March 30, 2009

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter trial comparing APTIOM 400, 800, and 1200 mg once daily with placebo
pivotal_trials.population: Adult epilepsy patients with partial-onset seizures (with or without secondary generalization) not adequately controlled with 1 to 3 concomitant AEDs
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Standardized seizure frequency during the Maintenance Phase over 28 days
pivotal_trials.n: Placebo N=95, 800 mg N=88, 1200 mg N=87
pivotal_trials.result: LS mean seizures per 28 days: placebo 6.6, 800 mg 5.0 (p=0.047), 1200 mg 4.3 (p=0.001)

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter trial comparing APTIOM 800 and 1200 mg once daily with placebo; this was the only new pivotal efficacy study submitted in the resubmission, and a daily-entry (DE) diary was introduced in the then ongoing study

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (dose-related) include dizziness (20% at 800 mg, 28% at 1200 mg vs 9% placebo), somnolence (11%/18% vs 8%), nausea (10%/16% vs 5%), headache (13%/15% vs 9%), and diplopia (9%/11% vs 2%). Serious risks include suicidal behavior/ideation, serious dermatologic reactions (SJS), DRESS/multiorgan hypersensitivity, anaphylaxis/angioedema, and clinically significant hyponatremia (sodium <125 mEq/L in 1.0% at 800 mg and 1.5% at 1200 mg vs none on placebo).
target_moa: Eslicarbazepine acetate is a prodrug extensively converted to eslicarbazepine, the active metabolite responsible for therapeutic effects; its anticonvulsant activity is thought to involve inhibition of voltage-gated sodium channels.

advisory_committee.vote: Not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the safety profile is similar to that of other drugs approved for this indication.

description.text: Expanded partial-onset seizures indication to include pediatric patients 4 years of age and older

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for a change to the indicated patient population for Aptiom used as treatment of partial-onset seizures. Specifically, the indication for Aptiom is being expanded to include pediatric patients 4 years of age and older. In addition, this application provides for a 7 tablet professional sample for the 200 mg strength of Aptiom tablets.

summary.text: This NDA for eslicarbazepine acetate as adjunctive treatment of partial-onset seizures was originally submitted in 2009 but received a Complete Response letter on April 30, 2010; the February 11, 2013 resubmission (reviewed under Priority review) added a new controlled Study 304 and updated analyses of Studies 301 and 302, and was approved without referral to an advisory committee.

citations.quote: The February 11, 2013, submission constituted a complete response to our April 30, 2010, action letter.
36 studies were submitted in the first NDA cycle (original application 2009).
Study 304 is the only new pivotal efficacy study submitted in this cycle.
**Review Priority:** Priority
Your application for eslicarbazepine was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the safety profile is similar to that of other drugs approved for this indication.
